sentences.text: 2. The grievance of the petitioner is that though award under LA case No. 5/2020-21 was passed in favour of the petitioner and respondent No. 7 and 8 and other three owners, totaling an amount of Rs. 52,59,170/-, however, the authority has released the entire amount in favour of the respondent Nos. 7 and 8, ignoring the award.
3. Issue notice, returnable on 25.06.2025.

4. Mr. D Nath, learned Senior Government counsel accepts notice on behalf of respondent Nos. 2, 5 and 6 and Mr. R Talukdar, learned standing counsel for the NHIDCL accepts notice on behalf of respondent Nos. 1, 3 and 4.
However, extra copies of the writ petition, in required number, be furnished to the learned counsel.
Petitioner to take steps for service of notice upon the respondent Nos. 7 to 18 by way of registered post with A/D and by way of usual process within a period of five days from today.
In addition, petitioner is permitted to take steps through dasti, however, same should be routed through the Registry of this court.
Thereafter, the petitioner shall file an affidavit in proof of service.

5. From the instruction received by the learned Senior Government Advocate, Assam, it is seen that an award was passed in favour of the petitioner and the private respondents herein totaling Rs.
52,59,170/-.

However, after such award was passed, a hearing was taken by the CALA and an order was passed on 06.03.2023, whereby the name of the present petitioner was excluded from the benefit of compensation to be paid under Dag No. 437 of Annual Patta No. 14 Page No.# 5/5 which otherwise reflected in the original award.

6. In the prima-facie view of this court, the CALA, though may be entitled to take a decision as regards entitlement and claim of interested parties in terms of Section 3H(3), however, after passing of the award, if there is any dispute as regards apportionment, the course of action that can be taken is in terms of Section 3H(4).
However in the case in hand, the award was passed on 04.02.2021 and the impugned order was passed on 06.03.2023.

7. Having prima-facie satisfaction that the CALA had acted without jurisdiction by passing the impugned order dated 06.03.2023, it is provided that the amount already released in favour of the respondent Nos. 7 and 8 shall be subject to the outcome of the writ petition.
